intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming waters at 38–40°C are especially magical under a starlit or aurora-lit sky.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Visit local markets, bakeries, and heritage restaurants to understand Iceland's Viking food culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike passes obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vivid multicolored hills before reaching the famous natural pool where hot and cold streams mix perfectly.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange budget transport (Flybus or shared shuttle) to Reykjavik area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront accommodation. Settle in, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk along the nearby coastline to get your bearings. Explore the immediate beachfront area and enjoy the dramatic January coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Reykjavik (bus or rideshare) for a gentle first-night exploration of Laugavegur Street. Watch for northern lights from the harbor area after dark — January darkness begins early (~4pm), maximizing aurora viewing chances. Download an aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) to track activity.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport on arrival or grab a snack from a Keflavik convenience store
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at Keflavik Airport or a petrol station en route — hot dogs from N1 station (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (submarine sandwich shop on Laugavegur) — filling and affordable, around 1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January sunset is around 4:30pm. Aurora activity can begin as early as 6pm on clear nights. Check Vedur.is for cloud cover and aurora forecasts nightly. Dress in thermal layers — January temps average -1°C to 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior, small fee for tower ~1,000 ISK). Walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture along the harbor for panoramic winter views. Explore the old harbor district on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Reykjavik City Pond (Tjörnin) to see winter birds. Walk through the old town and browse the flea market at Kolaportið (open weekends, check schedule) for cheap local goods and food. Visit Austurvöllur square and the Althing parliament building exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt: take a free self-guided walk to Grótta Lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes peninsula (30-min bus ride from city center) — one of the best free aurora viewing spots near Reykjavik with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — buy groceries from Bónus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest chain) for bread, eggs, and skyr yogurt
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's most famous hot dog stand near the harbor, ~500 ISK per dog
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or soup from Bónus groceries at accommodation to save budget

day_by_day.notes: Bónus supermarket is the most budget-friendly grocery option in Iceland. Stock up on breakfast and lunch items to significantly reduce daily food costs. Grótta Lighthouse requires a 20-minute walk from the bus stop.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Golden Circle — book a budget shared group tour (from ~8,000–10,000 ISK) or rent a car if splitting costs with fellow travelers. First stop: Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, free entry) — walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle: visit the Geysir geothermal area (free entry) to witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — Iceland's most famous waterfall, spectacular even in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir if time permits (~3,000 ISK entry — cheaper than Blue Lagoon). Aurora watch from accommodation beachfront on return.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before early departure
meals.lunch: Pack a packed lunch from Bónus groceries to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss — saves significant money vs. tourist-area restaurants
meals.dinner: Mandi restaurant in Reykjavik — affordable Middle Eastern/Icelandic fusion, around 1,800–2,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle tours depart early (~8–9am). Book in advance online for best budget rates. Reykjavik Excursions and Gray Line offer shared budget tours. Roads may be icy — check road.is before travel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjavik Thermal Pools: Laugardalslaug (the largest public pool in Iceland, ~1,000 ISK entry) — enjoy the outdoor hot pots, steam rooms, and slides. This is where locals go and is far cheaper than commercial hot springs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Laugardalur Valley area: visit the free Botanical Garden (winter walking only), and the nearby Ásmundarsafn sculpture museum (small entry fee or free on certain days). Walk along the Elliðaár river valley trail.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights tour on foot: take Bus Route 1 to Öskjuhlíð hill and the Perlan museum area — elevated position with panoramic dark-sky views over Reykjavik. The surrounding Öskjuhlíð forest offers good aurora viewing spots.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — skyr with granola and coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Vinyl — vegan-friendly café in Reykjavik with affordable soups and sandwiches (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered stew or soup at accommodation using Bónus groceries

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug is a beloved local experience and one of the best budget activities in Iceland. Bring your own towel if possible (rental costs extra). January water temperatures in hot pots are around 38–42°C — perfect for cold evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula (accessible by bus or budget tour). Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge over the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift (free). Explore the dramatic volcanic lava fields and coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse) and the nearby Gunnuhver hot spring geothermal area — bubbling mud pools and steam vents (free entry). Walk the marked trails around the geothermal field.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. If skies are clear, the Reykjanes Peninsula has very low light pollution — consider staying later for aurora viewing before returning. Check aurora forecast before committing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bónus groceries eaten at Gunnuhver geothermal area
meals.dinner: Noodle Station in Reykjavik — popular budget spot, beef or vegetarian noodle soup ~1,500–1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly geologically active. Check for any volcanic activity advisories at almannavarnir.is before visiting. Some areas may be restricted. This peninsula was affected by volcanic activity in 2023–2024 — verify access conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls — book a budget South Coast shared tour (~10,000–12,000 ISK) or rent a car. Seljalandsfoss allows walking behind the waterfall (may be icy/closed in winter — check conditions). Both are free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue South Coast: visit Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks. Walk the beach carefully (sneaker waves are dangerous — stay back from the water). Explore the black sand dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Return along the South Coast. Stop at Skaftáreldahraun lava field viewpoint if light permits. Excellent aurora viewing from the South Coast due to minimal light pollution — plan to stop on the return drive if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bónus or stop at a petrol station N1/Orkan for budget soup and hot dogs (~800–1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation on return

day_by_day.notes: South Coast tours are long (10–12 hours). Dress in full waterproof gear — waterfalls create significant spray. Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. Ice crampons (meðferð) recommended for waterfall areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the beachfront accommodation. Walk the local coastline at your own pace, watching for seabirds and enjoying the winter seascape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik Maritime Museum (Sjóminjasafnið) — affordable entry (~2,000 ISK) with fascinating exhibits on Iceland's fishing heritage. Walk along the old harbor and watch fishing boats. Browse the Grandi harbor district's street art.
day_by_day.evening: Reykjavik's budget nightlife: visit a local bar during happy hour (5–7pm) for discounted drinks. Try Kaldi Bar or Micro Bar for Icelandic craft beers at reasonable prices. Early evening northern lights check from the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Extended self-catered breakfast at accommodation — eggs, toast, skyr
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters café — excellent coffee and affordable pastries/sandwiches (~1,200–1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Aktu Taktu fast food chain — Icelandic-style burgers and fries, very affordable (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for energy recovery. Use the afternoon to do laundry if needed, restock groceries at Bónus, and plan the second week of the trip. Check road conditions for upcoming day trips at road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Snæfellsnes Peninsula (long day trip — depart very early, 7am). Drive or join a budget tour to Snæfellsjökull glacier and national park. Visit Arnarstapi coastal village with dramatic lava arch formations (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsnes: visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) with rusted shipwreck remains. Drive to Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain — and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall (free). Golden hour light in January creates stunning photography conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Begin return drive to Reykjavik. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula has exceptional aurora viewing conditions — if skies are clear, pull over on the return drive for aurora photography. Arrive back at accommodation by 9–10pm.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before 7am departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bónus eaten at Djúpalónssandur beach
meals.dinner: Petrol station hot meal on return drive, or self-catered at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 2.5 hours from Reykjavik. This is a very long day — consider booking a guided budget tour to avoid driving fatigue. Tours run approximately 10,000–13,000 ISK. Road F-roads are closed in winter — stick to Route 54.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Plant (free visitor area, ~40 min from Reykjavik) — see Iceland's geothermal energy in action with massive steam columns. Drive through the Þingvellir area en route for a second, quieter visit to the national park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Almannagjá gorge trail in Þingvellir National Park (free) — walk the rift valley between tectonic plates in winter silence. Visit the Öxará river and the historic Law Rock (Lögberg). The park is dramatically beautiful with potential snow cover.
day_by_day.evening: Þingvellir has some of Iceland's darkest skies near Reykjavik — if aurora forecast is KP2 or higher, stay until dark (4:30pm onwards) for exceptional northern lights viewing over the lake (Þingvallavatn).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bónus eaten in Þingvellir National Park
meals.dinner: Self-catered warm meal at accommodation — soup or pasta

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir in winter is extraordinarily peaceful with few tourists. The lake Þingvallavatn sometimes partially freezes in January, creating beautiful ice formations. Bring ice grips for hiking — trails can be icy. Nesjavellir road is generally passable in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River — a 3km hike from the trailhead near Hveragerði (~45 min from Reykjavik). The hike leads to a natural hot river where you can bathe for free. One of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hveragerði town — Iceland's 'hot spring town' with geothermal greenhouses growing tomatoes and bananas. Visit the free geothermal park in the town center with bubbling hot springs and steam vents. Stop at a local greenhouse café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Visit Sundhöllin — the oldest swimming pool in Reykjavik, recently renovated, with rooftop hot tubs (entry ~1,000 ISK). Soak in the outdoor hot tubs under the night sky with potential aurora views.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — pack extra snacks for the hike
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from Bónus, eaten at Reykjadalur hot river after bathing
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar submarine sandwiches in Reykjavik — budget-friendly and filling (~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is moderately challenging and can be icy in January — microspikes/crampons are strongly recommended. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and dry bag for your clothes. The hike takes approximately 1.5 hours each way. Start early to maximize daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Perlan museum (exterior and free areas) on Öskjuhlíð hill for panoramic 360-degree views over Reykjavik. Walk the free observation deck. Explore the surrounding Öskjuhlíð forest trails — a hidden gem for locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum (Árbæjarsafn) — an outdoor folk museum showing traditional Icelandic turf houses and farm buildings (~2,000 ISK entry, or free on certain winter days). Walk through reconstructed 18th–19th century Icelandic village.
day_by_day.evening: Final major northern lights hunt: book a budget aurora minibus tour (~5,000–7,000 ISK) that drives away from city light pollution to optimal viewing locations based on that night's forecast. These tours include a guide and aurora guarantee on some operators.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Café Babalú in Reykjavik — cozy budget café with soups and sandwiches (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation before evening aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: Book the aurora tour in advance — January is peak season for northern lights tourism. Operators like Arctic Adventures, Reykjavik Excursions, and Guide to Iceland offer budget options. Many offer a free repeat tour if no aurora is seen on the first attempt.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite spots. Morning walk along the Reykjavik coastal path (Ægissíðuvegur) — a free 4km seaside walking trail with views of Mount Esja and the Snæfellsnes glacier on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — comprehensive Icelandic history from settlement to present (~2,000 ISK, free on certain days). Spend 2–3 hours exploring Viking artifacts, medieval church art, and modern Icelandic culture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik. Treat yourself slightly within budget. Browse Laugavegur street one final time, pick up any souvenirs from the Kolaportið flea market or charity shops (cheapest souvenirs). Final aurora check from the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Snaps Bistro or Café Haiti in the harbor area — affordable and authentic (~1,800–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Treat meal: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers on the harbor, ~2,500–3,500 ISK — a splurge-worthy budget farewell

day_by_day.notes: The Sægreifinn lobster soup (humarsúpa) is considered one of the best budget food experiences in Iceland at approximately 1,500 ISK per bowl. The harbor location also offers excellent aurora viewing after dinner if skies are clear.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning: check out of accommodation. Pack carefully and store luggage if checkout is before airport transfer. Take a final walk along the beachfront at your accommodation to say goodbye to the Icelandic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange Flybus or shared shuttle transfer to Keflavik International Airport (book in advance — departs ~2.5 hours before flight). Allow extra time for potential icy road conditions. Do final duty-free shopping at Keflavik Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 days of northern lights, hot springs, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at accommodation using remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Airport meal at Keflavik — budget options available at the terminal (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Flybus to Keflavik costs approximately 3,500–4,500 ISK one way. Book return transfer in advance at re.is. Check flight details carefully — Keflavik Airport (KEF) is 50km from Reykjavik. Allow 3 hours minimum before international departure for check-in, security, and potential weather delays.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming waters at 38–40°C are especially magical under a starlit or aurora-lit sky.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely walk along the shoreline to get your bearings and breathe in the crisp Icelandic coastal air. Stop at a nearby viewpoint to watch the winter light fade over the Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 20 minutes from Keflavik area) for a relaxing evening soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters — perfect after a long flight. Pre-book the Comfort package to include a welcome drink and silica mud mask.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby café upon arrival — try Kef Bistro at the airport for a bowl of Icelandic lamb soup
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — mid-range set menu featuring Icelandic fish and lamb dishes with geothermal views

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking the Blue Lagoon is essential — slots fill up weeks in advance. January sunset is around 16:30, so the evening soak will be beautifully lit by darkness and steam.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the resort, drive or take a guided tour to the Reykjanes Peninsula. Explore the dramatic lava fields, fumaroles, and the Bridge Between Continents — a walkway spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Visit the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Grindavik town for a stroll and local exploration. Visit the Saltfish Museum to learn about Iceland's fishing heritage. Return to the resort for a short rest before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join a small-group guided jeep tour departing from the Reykjavik/Reykjanes area into the dark countryside to chase the aurora borealis away from light pollution. Tour typically runs 21:00–01:00.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy skyr, Icelandic rye bread, smoked salmon, and eggs
meals.lunch: Bryggjan Brugghús in Grindavik — a local craft brewery and café serving fish and chips and hearty sandwiches
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the Northern Lights tour at Salthúsið Restaurant in Grindavik — fresh seafood and Icelandic lamb stew

day_by_day.notes: Dress in thermal layers for the Northern Lights jeep tour — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below. The guide will monitor aurora forecasts throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late Northern Lights tour. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Mid-morning, drive to Reykjavik (about 45–50 minutes) and explore the iconic Hallgrímskirkja Church — take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Laugavegur, Reykjavik's main shopping street. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront for its stunning geometric glass architecture. Pop into the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) to learn about Iceland's Viking origins.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's cozy restaurant scene for dinner, then return to the resort. Keep an eye on aurora alerts via the Icelandic Met Office app — if the KP index is favorable, step outside the resort for a spontaneous Northern Lights viewing from the dark beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — try traditional Icelandic flatbread with smoked trout and hangikjöt (smoked lamb)
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik — renowned for their cast-iron skillets of fresh Icelandic fish at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik parking is limited — consider using the Strætó bus system or a rideshare app for city navigation. The Settlement Exhibition costs around 2,200 ISK per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the famous Golden Circle route. Start with Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can walk between the tectonic plates and see the original Viking parliament site. Arrive early to enjoy the serene winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Then drive to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall, Iceland's most iconic two-tiered cascade — stunning in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort via the southern route. If aurora conditions are favorable, pull over in a dark rural area for Northern Lights viewing. Back at the resort, warm up in any available hot tub or geothermal pool on property.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — pack a snack for the road
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café — convenient stop for lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate between geothermal sights
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Restaurant near Reykholt — a unique greenhouse restaurant serving tomato-based dishes grown on-site; book in advance

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Roads may be icy — check road conditions at road.is before departing. Bring microspikes for walking on icy paths at Þingvellir.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Ring Road to the South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — in summer you can walk behind it, but in January enjoy the frozen curtain of ice and dramatic spray from a safe distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic falls. Climb the staircase to the right for elevated views over the coastline. Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — admire the basalt sea stacks (Reynisdrangar) and the thundering Atlantic surf.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or continue back toward the resort area. Stop at the village of Vík for dinner before returning. If staying overnight near Vík, position yourself for a potential Northern Lights sighting over the black beach.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort before departing
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — seafood chowder and lamb burgers with views of Reynisfjara
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi in Vík — cozy local restaurant known for lamb dishes and fish of the day at reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back to the ocean at Reynisfjara — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous and have caused fatalities. Obey all warning signs and stay behind the safety markers.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 2.5 hours east of Vík). Watch icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier drift silently across the lagoon in otherworldly blue hues — especially magical in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Diamond Beach directly across the road — a black sand beach strewn with translucent ice chunks washed ashore, glittering like diamonds. Explore the nearby Fjallsárlón Glacier Lagoon for a quieter, equally beautiful alternative. Begin the drive back westward.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Skaftafell Nature Reserve for a short winter walk if daylight permits. Continue back toward the resort or overnight near Kirkjubæjarklaustur. Northern Lights watch from the road on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Vík accommodation or packed from the resort
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Café (seasonal — confirm availability in January) or packed lunch from a Vík supermarket
meals.dinner: Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a beloved local café serving hearty Icelandic meals including lamb soup and fish dishes

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 375 km from Reykjavik — this is a long driving day (5+ hours total). Consider splitting into two days or joining a guided South Coast + Glacier Lagoon day tour for comfort and safety on icy roads.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning exploring the beachfront — look for seabirds, dramatic wave formations, and enjoy the solitude of the Icelandic winter coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) at Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891, a natural hot spring pool surrounded by geothermal activity and a small geyser. The rustic, uncrowded atmosphere is a wonderful contrast to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a quiet evening. Enjoy dinner at the resort restaurant. Set an aurora alarm for midnight — January often brings strong KP index nights. The dark beachfront location is ideal for Northern Lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time
meals.lunch: Light meal at the Secret Lagoon café or pack a picnic
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant at Aegean Bliss — enjoy a beachfront dinner with Icelandic fish or lamb specialties

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is about 1.5 hours from the Reykjanes area. Entry costs approximately 3,000 ISK per adult. The pool stays at a consistent 38–40°C year-round — blissful in the cold January air.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north toward Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2 hours from Reykjavik). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and see the rusted shipwreck remains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks and the Arnarstapi coastal cliffs with their sea arches and nesting bird colonies. Drive through the charming fishing village of Grundarfjörður with views of the iconic Kirkjufell mountain — one of Iceland's most photographed peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Kirkjufell is an exceptional Northern Lights location — if the aurora is active, the mountain with its twin waterfalls (Kirkjufellsfoss) creates an iconic foreground. Return to the resort late evening.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café at Hellnar — a charming seaside café known for fish soup and waffles with cream and jam; one of Iceland's most beloved hidden gems
meals.dinner: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — excellent seafood and lamb in a cozy setting overlooking Kirkjufell

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is called 'Iceland in Miniature' as it showcases nearly every Icelandic landscape type in one peninsula. Roads can be challenging — check conditions at road.is. The drive back is about 2.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Westfjords border area or the Borgarfjörður region. Visit Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring — where water boils at 100°C and billows steam dramatically into the cold winter air. Nearby Reykholt village has historical connections to medieval saga writer Snorri Sturluson.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls — Hraunfossar is a series of rivulets emerging from under a lava field and flowing into the Hvítá River, particularly beautiful in winter with ice formations. A short drive away, Barnafoss features a dramatic gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner and an aurora watch session from the beachfront. January's long nights maximize your chances — aim to stay up until at least midnight on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Húsafell Resort restaurant near Hraunfossar — warm soups and sandwiches in a scenic woodland setting
meals.dinner: Þorpið Restaurant in Borgarnes — local favorite for Icelandic meat soup and fresh fish; try the Settlement Center's restaurant for a themed Viking dinner experience

day_by_day.notes: The Settlement Center in Borgarnes has an excellent exhibition on Iceland's settlement history and the Egils Saga — worth a 1-hour visit in the afternoon if time allows. Entry around 2,400 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Northern Lights photography and hunting morning — review last night's aurora activity and plan the day around tonight's forecast. Morning visit to the Reykjanes Geopark volcanic landscapes near the resort — explore lava tubes, craters, and steaming vents on a self-guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse (Valahnúkamöl) — Iceland's oldest lighthouse area with dramatic coastal cliffs and crashing waves. The surrounding area has striking volcanic rock formations and is excellent for photography in the low winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour — if you didn't see the aurora on Day 2 or want another attempt, this is your dedicated second booking. Alternatively, if aurora conditions are strong, drive independently to a dark spot on the Reykjanes Peninsula for a self-guided viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Berg Restaurant in Keflavik — a mid-range option serving fresh fish, burgers, and Icelandic classics
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Suðurnes Science and Learning Center café, or pack a thermos of hot chocolate for the Northern Lights tour

day_by_day.notes: Download the 'Aurora Forecast' app and set alerts for KP index 3 or above. The Reykjanes Peninsula's flat, open terrain and proximity to the ocean makes it one of the best aurora-viewing areas in southwest Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) — a world-class gallery in a beautiful park setting featuring Icelandic art. Then walk through the Tjörnin lake area in central Reykjavik to feed the ducks and admire the colorful city hall reflected in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times. Afterward, browse the flea market at Kolaportið (open weekends) or explore independent boutiques on Skólavörðustígur street for Icelandic wool sweaters and local design.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Reykjavik's vibrant food scene with a progressive dinner — start with drinks and small plates at a wine bar, then move to a main course restaurant. Return to the resort and enjoy a final hot spring soak if the property has facilities.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Sandholt Bakery in Reykjavik — Iceland's finest artisan bakery with sourdough, pastries, and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — a beloved Reykjavik institution serving grilled langoustine skewers and fish soup at very reasonable prices directly from the harbor
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant) — upscale-casual Icelandic-Asian fusion; slightly above mid-range but worth it for a special evening; try the sashimi and Arctic char

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market is only open Saturdays and Sundays — check if this falls on a weekend. The National Museum is closed on Mondays. Reykjavik is very walkable — most city center attractions are within 15–20 minutes on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — return to the Blue Lagoon for a morning soak with a different atmosphere than your evening visit on Day 1. Book the Premium package this time to include a floating breakfast in the water and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, drive to the Krýsuvík geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula — a raw, steaming landscape of colorful sulfurous mud pools, fumaroles, and boiling vents. The vivid yellows, reds, and greens against the black lava are extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik. Spend the evening on Laugavegur for last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Icelandic chocolate, schnapps (Brennivín), and lopapeysa wool sweaters. Return to resort for packing and an early night.

meals.breakfast: Floating breakfast experience at the Blue Lagoon (included in Premium package) — sparkling wine, fresh fruit, and pastries in the geothermal waters
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon café or grab a sandwich from a Keflavik supermarket
meals.dinner: Grillið at Hotel Saga in Reykjavik — a rooftop restaurant with panoramic city views and excellent Icelandic lamb and seafood; a memorable farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Premium package well in advance — it sells out quickly. Krýsuvík requires a short walk on uneven terrain — wear sturdy boots and stay on marked paths as the ground can be unstable near geothermal features.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack and check out. If your flight is in the afternoon, take a short final walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to the Icelandic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 15–20 minutes from the resort area). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up Icelandic duty-free spirits and chocolates as final souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of geothermal wonders, aurora chasing, volcanic landscapes, and Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — savor the skyr and smoked salmon one last time
meals.lunch: Airport restaurants at Keflavik — Fljótt og Gott offers quick Icelandic sandwiches and soup; or splurge on a final bowl of lobster bisque at the airport's sit-down restaurant
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight time and arrange airport transfer the night before. The Blue Lagoon offers a convenient luggage storage service if you want a final soak before departing — book the 'Stopover' package which is designed specifically for departing travelers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming waters at 38–40°C are especially magical under a starlit or aurora-lit sky.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Visit local markets, bakeries, and heritage restaurants to understand Iceland's Viking food culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike passes obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vivid multicolored hills before reaching the famous natural pool where hot and cold streams mix perfectly.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing at Keflavík International Airport, a private luxury transfer awaits to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront suite and enjoy a welcome amenity.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely orientation walk along the beachfront property. Visit the resort's private geothermal pool or spa to decompress from travel. Explore the resort amenities and enjoy a curated welcome drink with panoramic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booked premium package) — located just minutes from the resort, this iconic milky-blue geothermal experience is perfect for the first evening. Enjoy the Lava Restaurant within the Blue Lagoon complex for dinner, featuring refined Icelandic cuisine with views over the steaming waters.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the resort upon check-in — charcuterie, Icelandic cheeses, smoked lamb, and skyr parfait
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, Arctic char, and slow-roasted lamb with local herb accompaniments

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package (premium tier) well in advance as slots fill quickly. Private airport transfer should be arranged ahead of arrival. January sunset is around 16:00, so the evening lagoon visit will be beautifully atmospheric under dark winter skies.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely luxury breakfast at the resort. Afterward, embark on a private guided tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula — explore dramatic lava fields, the Bridge Between Continents (spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), and the Gunnuhver geothermal mud pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse and the rugged coastal cliffs. Stop at the Krýsuvík geothermal area to witness steaming fumaroles and colorful mineral deposits. Return to the resort for a private spa treatment — choose from hot stone massage or a silica mud facial inspired by the geothermal landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — depart from the resort with a small-group expert guide into the dark countryside of the Reykjanes Peninsula and beyond. Your guide will use aurora forecasting apps and local knowledge to find the best viewing spots away from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast buffet at the resort — freshly baked rúgbrauð (dark rye bread), smoked salmon, skyr, Icelandic cheeses, and free-range eggs
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic prepared by the resort chef — enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint on the Reykjanes Peninsula
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur restaurant in Reykjavik (30-min drive) — celebrated for reinvented traditional Icelandic recipes; try the cod's head and fermented shark tasting flight

day_by_day.notes: January is peak aurora season with long dark nights (up to 19 hours of darkness). Dress in thermal layers for the jeep tour — the resort concierge can provide high-quality outerwear if needed. Aurora activity is weather-dependent; the guide will reschedule if cloud cover is heavy.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes volcanic landscape — witness active fissures, steaming vents, and the dramatic coastline from above. This exclusive aerial perspective of Iceland's newest lava flows is a truly once-in-a-lifetime luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour in Reykjavik — join a premium small-group culinary tour through the capital's vibrant food scene. Sample traditional dishes including skyr varieties, hákarl (fermented shark), pylsur (Icelandic hot dogs), kleinur pastries, and local craft beers and spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's Laugavegur street for boutique Icelandic design shopping. Dine at one of Iceland's finest restaurants for a multi-course tasting menu experience.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with crowberry jam, Skyr mousse, and freshly brewed Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Included in the Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour — a progressive feast across multiple Reykjavik establishments
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a Nordic tasting menu with paired wine or non-alcoholic botanical beverage flight

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour and Dill Restaurant well in advance as both require reservations. The food tour typically lasts 3–4 hours and covers significant ground in Reykjavik's city center. Comfortable waterproof boots are recommended for walking tours in January.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private 4x4 vehicle for the famous Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. In winter, the frost-covered landscape is ethereally beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–40 meters into the air. Proceed to Gullfoss Waterfall — Iceland's most powerful waterfall, partially frozen in January, creating a dramatic ice sculpture effect.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. En route, stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating to 1891. Soak under the winter sky with potential aurora views overhead. Return to the resort for a private in-room dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast box prepared by the resort — smoked salmon bagel, skyr cup, fruit, and thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Geysir — dine in a working tomato greenhouse; famous for their tomato soup, tomato bread, and tomato cocktails (unique and memorable)
meals.dinner: Private in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — three-course curated menu featuring pan-seared Arctic char, truffle mashed potatoes, and a warm skyr soufflé

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the Reykjanes area — plan for a full day. January roads can be icy; ensure your private driver has a certified 4x4. The Secret Lagoon is less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic, rustic experience. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation morning at the resort. Enjoy a private yoga session on the beachfront (arranged by the concierge) followed by a full spa treatment — choose a geothermal stone therapy massage or a premium body wrap using Icelandic mineral-rich products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snowmobile excursion on a glacier near the Reykjanes area or a guided ice cave exploration tour (subject to guide availability and conditions). Experience Iceland's frozen interior in a thrilling and exclusive way.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second attempt or first if previous was clouded out) — your expert guide will take you to new locations based on the latest aurora forecast. Enjoy hot chocolate and Icelandic pastries under the stars while waiting for the lights to dance.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — Icelandic oatmeal with cloudberry compote, freshly baked sourdough, smoked lamb, and a selection of herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled langoustine skewers, avocado and smoked salmon tartine, and sparkling water with Icelandic herbs
meals.dinner: Slippbarinn at Icelandair Hotel Reykjavik Marina — vibrant cocktail bar and restaurant known for creative Icelandic small plates and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile and ice cave tours must be booked through the resort concierge in advance. Glacier activities require appropriate safety gear, provided by the tour operator. The second jeep tour increases your chances of seeing the aurora if the first was weather-affected.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided whale watching tour from Reykjavik Old Harbour (approximately 40-minute drive from the resort). January offers sightings of humpback whales, minke whales, and white-beaked dolphins. Opt for a premium small-boat tour for a more intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik Art Museum and the Harpa Concert Hall — Iceland's stunning glass concert venue on the harbor waterfront. Attend a guided architectural tour of Harpa and browse the gift shop for high-end Icelandic design pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music or traditional Icelandic music concert at Harpa Concert Hall (check schedule for January 2027 programming). Afterward, dine at one of Reykjavik's top waterfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked trout on rye crispbread, poached eggs, skyr with Icelandic honey, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Kopar Restaurant at Reykjavik Old Harbour — seafood-focused menu with harbor views; try the langoustine soup and grilled catfish
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — an exclusive 12-seat chef's table experience offering a surprise tasting menu; one of Iceland's most intimate and celebrated dining experiences (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January can be cold and rough — dress in full thermal gear. The tour operator provides overalls and life vests. Óx Restaurant has extremely limited seating and should be booked months in advance. Harpa concert tickets should also be purchased ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast — depart by private 4x4 to Seljalandsfoss Waterfall, where in summer you can walk behind the falls (in January it may be partially iced over but equally spectacular). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall with its iconic double rainbow effect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach of Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns and crashing Atlantic waves. Explore the nearby Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Continue to the village of Vík for a brief exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop for dinner in the charming town of Selfoss. Afterward, keep an eye on aurora forecasts — if conditions are favorable, your driver can stop at a dark-sky location on the return journey for spontaneous northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — packed gourmet thermos of soup and sandwiches for the road
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — cozy restaurant serving traditional Icelandic lamb soup, fresh fish, and homemade cakes with views of the black sand beach
meals.dinner: Tryggvaskáli Restaurant in Selfoss — housed in a historic building, serving elevated Icelandic cuisine with local lamb and fresh river fish

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is approximately 150–200 km from the resort. January roads can be challenging — a certified 4x4 driver is essential. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves; stay well back from the water's edge. Sunset is around 16:00, so plan to be at Reynisfjara before dark for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike (winter-accessible version via super jeep) — depart early with a specialist highland guide in a powerful super jeep. Trek through the stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains of the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and soak in the natural geothermal hot springs surrounded by snow-dusted mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Landmannalaugar area — hike to viewpoints overlooking the obsidian lava fields and steaming geothermal vents. Your guide will provide hot drinks and Icelandic snacks during the excursion. Return journey through the dramatic highland landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a restorative evening. Enjoy a private in-resort spa session — geothermal mineral bath and full-body massage. Light room service dinner to rest after the active day.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast before departure — porridge with Icelandic honey, eggs, smoked meats, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the resort — thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot tea
meals.dinner: In-room dining at the resort — slow-cooked Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée, fresh bread, and a selection from the resort's premium wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires a specialized super jeep with experienced highland drivers — standard vehicles cannot access the area in winter. This is a full-day excursion (10–12 hours). Bring extra layers, waterproof clothing, and a swimsuit for the hot spring soak. The combination of snow and geothermal steam in winter is extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort. Enjoy a private cooking class with the resort's executive chef — learn to prepare traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr-based desserts, rúgbrauð baked in geothermal ground, and cured fish preparations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark — explore the visitor center to understand Iceland's unique geological history. Take a guided walk through the Bridge Between Continents area with a geologist guide for an in-depth explanation of tectonic plate activity.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (third opportunity) — venture into the darkest areas of the Reykjanes Peninsula and surrounding highlands. Your guide will have identified optimal locations based on the aurora forecast. Enjoy warming Icelandic schnapps (brennivín) and pastries during the hunt.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked croissants, Icelandic butter, smoked salmon, and a smoothie bar with Icelandic berries
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — a shared lunch of the dishes prepared during the morning session, served in the resort's private dining room
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavik — rooftop fine dining with panoramic city views, known for premium Icelandic beef and seafood tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be pre-arranged with the resort concierge. January aurora forecasts can be checked via the Icelandic Meteorological Office app (Vedur). The brennivín tasting during the jeep tour is optional — non-alcoholic alternatives are always available.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing expedition in the Reykjanes lava fields — guided by a local expert, explore the otherworldly frozen lava landscape on snowshoes. The winter silence and stark beauty of the volcanic terrain is unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Icelandic Lava Show in Reykjavik — a unique live demonstration where real molten lava is poured and you can experience the heat, sound, and spectacle of a volcanic eruption up close in a safe indoor setting.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dining experience — arrange through the resort concierge for a private chef to prepare a bespoke Icelandic tasting menu in your suite or a private resort dining room, paired with wines selected by a sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked Icelandic salmon on rúgbrauð, fresh fruit platter, and freshly squeezed Arctic berry juice
meals.lunch: Café Loki, Reykjavik — traditional Icelandic café famous for hearty lamb soup, rye bread ice cream, and hákarl tasting; an authentic and beloved local spot
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner — seven-course tasting menu featuring Icelandic lobster bisque, cured Arctic char, skyr sorbet palate cleanser, slow-roasted reindeer, artisan Icelandic cheese board, and volcanic salt dark chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe equipment is provided by the tour guide. The Lava Show is a ticketed attraction and should be booked in advance — approximately 30–45 minutes in duration. The private chef dinner is the highlight of the trip's dining experiences and should be arranged with the resort at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5-hour drive by private 4x4) — explore the mystical Snæfellsjökull glacier and volcano, immortalized in Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Visit the glacier's edge with a certified glacier guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi and the dramatic coastal cliffs of Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach. Visit the Snæfellsnes National Park visitor center and the iconic Kirkjufell mountain — one of Iceland's most photographed landmarks.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward the resort. If aurora conditions are favorable, your driver will stop at a prime dark-sky location on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for a spontaneous northern lights experience far from any light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — packed gourmet provisions for the long drive including thermos of coffee, pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Hótel Búðir Restaurant — one of Iceland's most romantic and remote restaurants, set in a historic black church landscape; famous for their Snæfellsnes lamb and fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant), Reykjavik — on the return journey; acclaimed sushi and Icelandic seafood fusion restaurant with an extensive sake and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a long day trip — depart by 08:00 to maximize daylight hours. The glacier visit requires crampons and safety equipment provided by the guide. Hótel Búðir restaurant reservation is essential and should be booked in advance. The return to the resort will be late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final Blue Lagoon experience — return to the Blue Lagoon for a premium Retreat Spa day package, including exclusive access to the private Retreat Lagoon (adults-only, quieter, and more luxurious), a signature silica mud mask treatment, and in-water floating massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the resort — pack, relax, and enjoy the resort's facilities one last time. Optional: browse the resort boutique for premium Icelandic souvenirs including wool knitwear (lopapeysa), volcanic salt, Icelandic spirits, and skincare products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants — a celebratory multi-course meal to commemorate an extraordinary 13-day Icelandic adventure.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread including all Icelandic favorites: skyr, smoked fish, rye bread, lamb, eggs, and pastries
meals.lunch: Moss Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa — exclusive restaurant accessible only to Retreat guests; refined Nordic tasting menu with geothermal views
meals.dinner: Geysir Restaurant at Fosshotel Reykjavik — panoramic rooftop views over Reykjavik with an elevated Icelandic tasting menu featuring locally sourced seasonal ingredients and a curated Icelandic wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Retreat Spa at Blue Lagoon is the premium tier experience and requires advance booking — it is significantly more exclusive and less crowded than the standard Blue Lagoon. This is your final full evening in Iceland; consider purchasing Icelandic souvenirs at the Blue Lagoon's boutique or in Reykjavik's Laugavegur street.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast and check out. Depending on your departure flight time, there may be time for one final soak in the resort's geothermal pool or a short walk along the beachfront to soak in the Icelandic coastal atmosphere one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Arrive with ample time for premium lounge access and duty-free shopping — pick up Icelandic spirits (brennivín), Nói Síríus chocolates, and lopapeysa wool sweaters as final mementos.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you extraordinary memories of northern lights dancing overhead, geothermal waters warming your bones, and the raw, elemental beauty of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a leisurely and indulgent spread; take your time and savor every last bite of Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or a quick farewell meal at Keflavík Airport — try the airport's Icelandic restaurant for a final bowl of lamb soup before departure
meals.dinner: On the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 — confirm with the resort and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the afternoon. Keflavík Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Reykjanes resort area. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Ensure all aurora photos are backed up before departure!
